title: The Fox Wedding
text: Rain falls from a clear sky, warm as tears. Through the wood comes a procession of foxes in silk walking upright, carrying lanterns and a bride in a red veil. It is very bad luck, the old wives say, to be seen watching.

options.label: Look away and hide, and pray the foxes never knew you were there.

outcomes.text: They pass. The rain stops. Where the procession walked you find a dropped wedding gift: a silk purse, heavy.
They pass. The rain stops. One fox turns back, looks right at your hiding place, and smiles. It will remember you.

options.label: Leave a gift for the fox bride, as the old wives say you should.

outcomes.text: A fox comes back alone, in silk, with a gift of its own, and bows. Luck follows you out of the wood.

options.label: The stealthiest watches the procession, curious where the foxes walk.

outcomes.text: Unseen, and they learn the foxes' secret road.
Seen. The bride lifts her veil, and smiles, and there is nothing beneath it but teeth.
